candidates.name: SajanGaba/zacks_scraper
candidates.what_it_holds: Python scraper (R3.py) for Zacks Investment Research plus one committed snapshot file R300.csv covering Russell 3000-style universe; ~14 fields per company including forward sales/earnings estimates, PE/PEG, and earnings-surprise history. Single point-in-time snapshot, not a repeated vintage series; no date metadata confirmed on the file itself.
candidates.why_useful: Closest thing found to a free, machine-pullable Zacks consensus-estimate scraper with a working example output; could be re-run at guide dates going forward to start building a point-in-time consensus series for ABNB per rule #2 (gap #4), though it captures no ABNB history retroactively.
candidates.time_coverage: single scrape snapshot, no historical run confirmed
candidates.size_hint: one CSV (R300.csv), unknown row count, small repo

candidates.name: igalci/zacks-scraper
candidates.what_it_holds: Small Python package (zacks_scraper/scraper.py) for pulling data from zacks.com; Apache-2.0 licensed; no data files committed, code only.
candidates.why_useful: A cleaner, packaged alternative Zacks-pulling method if the team wants to start a forward point-in-time Zacks consensus capture for ABNB/BKNG/EXPE; would need to be run going forward, contributes nothing retroactive.

candidates.name: DerekZhang0000/ZackScraper
candidates.what_it_holds: Node.js scraper compiling Zacks' "top recommended stocks" rank changes; a stock-screener/rating scraper, not an EPS-estimate history extractor.
candidates.why_useful: Marginal: Zacks Rank changes are a coarse revision-direction signal, not usable for ABNB EPS estimate history directly, but shows a working scrape pattern against Zacks pages if the team wants ABNB-specific rank tracking going forward.

candidates.name: QuantConnect/Lean.DataSource.Estimize
candidates.what_it_holds: C# reference implementation (DataProcessing/, EstimizeConsensus.cs, EstimizeEstimate.cs, EstimizeRelease.cs) showing how QuantConnect's Lean platform ingests Estimize's Estimates/Releases/Consensus data types. No underlying Estimize data is committed to the repo — it is a schema/pipeline example only, and the actual Estimize feed is a paid QuantConnect Data Marketplace product.
candidates.why_useful: Documents the exact schema (per-company consensus, individual crowd estimates, releases) an I/B/E/S-like Estimize feed would have if the team later pays for or otherwise obtains Estimize data; not itself a free data source.

candidates.name: bvb-06/WebScraping-Estimize
candidates.what_it_holds: MIT-licensed scraper targeting estimize.com for EPS/analyst-crowd estimates; repo content not deeply inspected beyond listing (small, likely code-only).
candidates.why_useful: Another working pattern for pulling Estimize's public estimate pages if the team wants forward point-in-time capture of crowd-sourced ABNB estimates.

candidates.name: ner-aim/Retreving-Financial-Estimates-using-Estimize
candidates.what_it_holds: Project retrieving FY2019 financial estimates for a handful of companies via Estimize; scope is a small fixed set of tickers/one fiscal year, not confirmed to include ABNB (which IPO'd Dec 2020, after FY2019).
candidates.why_useful: Low direct relevance (predates ABNB's public listing) but shows another Estimize-pulling method; mainly useful as a code pattern.

candidates.name: suranjana58/EstimizeScraping_DB
candidates.what_it_holds: Selenium/pandas scraper of Estimize tables into a database, with querying/analysis notebooks; content and coverage not verified beyond the description.
candidates.why_useful: Another Estimize scraping pattern (Selenium-based, useful if Estimize's site requires JS rendering); no confirmed committed dataset.

candidates.name: jordanhauer4/Estimize-API
candidates.what_it_holds: Simple Python client wrapping the (former) public Estimize Community Data API — a documented REST endpoint rather than a page scraper.
candidates.why_useful: If Estimize's community API endpoint still resolves, this is a lower-maintenance pull method than HTML scraping for forward point-in-time ABNB crowd-estimate capture; API may be dead (2015-era client) so needs a live check before relying on it.

candidates.name: KFoxder/Estimize_Data
candidates.what_it_holds: Old (2014) repo named 'Estimize_Data'; README fetch returned 404 (default branch/file naming may differ, e.g. master vs main, or README absent) so contents could not be confirmed remotely without cloning.
candidates.why_useful: Name suggests a committed Estimize dataset from ~2014; worth a human clone-and-look given how rare committed historical-estimate data is, but unverified and very old.

candidates.name: ishasolanki04/bharat-estimize-
candidates.what_it_holds: "BharatEstimize" — an AI-powered consensus-trading strategy for Indian equities; framed as a strategy repo, not a raw historical-estimate dataset. Likely uses live/paid data feeds internally.
candidates.why_useful: Not directly relevant (Indian equities, strategy not data), included only because it demonstrates a consensus/estimate-revision trading construction pattern that could be adapted; essentially not useful for ABNB.

notes: Hard 6-call gh-search-repos budget was used on: (1) combined 'zacks scraper'+'earnings estimates' [empty — gh search repos ANDs all quoted terms and is very strict], (2) 'estimize', (3) 'analyst estimates history' [empty], (4) 'zacks scraper', (5) 'IBES estimates' [empty], (6) 'EPS estimate revisions' [empty]. Broad terms like 'IBES', 'estimate revisions', and 'analyst estimates history' return nothing on GitHub's repo-search — this space is genuinely thin on GitHub: essentially no committed I/B/E/S-like open datasets exist publicly (I/B/E/S/Refinitiv data is licensed and basically never redistributed openly, which matches CONTEXT.md gap #4 being flagged as high-value/hard). What exists is almost entirely small, unmaintained, one-person SCRAPER repos (Estimize, Zacks) with little to no committed historical data — most are 0-3 stars, single-purpose, several years stale. The one exception with an actual committed data file is SajanGaba/zacks_scraper (R300.csv), but it is a single snapshot, not a vintage/point-in-time series, so it does not by itself solve gap #4 — it would need to be re-run repeatedly starting now to build a forward-looking point-in-time series (consistent with rule #2 in AGENT_BRIEF/CONTEXT: point-in-time-or-it-doesn't-count). Did not find any Finviz-specific scraper repos worth flagging (search terms exhausted before reaching Finviz specifically), nor any Alpha Vantage earnings-estimates-history dataset repos (Alpha Vantage's EARNINGS_ESTIMATES-type free endpoint is thin and generic API-wrapper repos dominated any query, none data-bearing). WebSearch quota was exhausted session-wide (shared across other scout agents) after 3 queries, cutting short the Finviz/Alpha-Vantage/general-EPS-revision-dataset web searches; a rerun with fresh WebSearch budget targeting 'finviz analyst estimates scraper github', 'alpha vantage EARNINGS_ESTIMATES github dataset', and 'wsj analyst estimates scraper github' would likely be worthwhile. Recommend a different modality (Socrata/CKAN-style academic data search, or Zenodo/Kaggle search) for this theme going forward, since GitHub itself appears to hold almost no redistributable historical consensus-estimate data — the realistic path to gap #4 is standing up one of these scrapers now and running it forward at each guide date, not finding a backfilled historical file.
